prompt: Find where the smallest value lives. Complete the indexOfMin method so it returns the index of the smallest element, preferring the first occurrence on ties and returning -1 for an empty array.
explanation: After guarding against the empty array, the method assumes index 0 holds the minimum and scans the rest of the array. Using a strict less-than comparison (values[i] < values[minIndex]) means a later element that merely ties never replaces the current winner, which is exactly the first-occurrence rule. Tracking the index instead of the value gives the answer directly.
hints: Handle the empty array first: if values.length == 0, return -1 immediately.
Keep a variable minIndex starting at 0 and compare each values[i] against values[minIndex].
Use < rather than <= so ties keep the earlier index.
